history.dynasty: None — built in modern times by the Birla family (B.D. Birla) through the Hindustan Charity Trust
history.summary: Foundation stone laid in 1960 by Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Dr. Kailashnath Katju and inaugurated in 1964 by Chief Minister Dwarka Prasad Mishra. The sandy-yellow Nagar-style temple stands on the highest point of the Arera Hills (Lakshminarayana Giri) in Malviya Nagar, south of the lake, offering a panoramic view of Bhopal. An attached museum (Birla Museum) displays 12th-century Paramara-period sculptures from Raisen, Sehore, Mandsaur and Shahdol districts. FLAG: CSV rows 539 (Lakshmi Narayan Temple) and 540 (Birla Mandir) are duplicate rows for this same temple. One web source (agatetravel.com) claims Mahatma Gandhi inaugurated it, which is chronologically implausible since the temple was founded in 1960 — likely a conflation with the Delhi Birla Mandir.

name: Lakshmi Narayan Temple
town_description: Bhopal, the capital of Madhya Pradesh, is known as the City of Lakes for its two artificial lakes (Upper and Lower) built centuries ago. It is one of India's greenest cities, blending Nawabi heritage — mosques, palaces and bazaars — with modern institutions and museums.

travel.airport: Raja Bhoj International Airport, Bhopal (~13 km; verify)
travel.road: Situated in the Malviya Nagar area on the Arera Hills, well connected by city roads, buses and auto-rickshaws

visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM to 12:00 PM and 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM (verify)
